text: [clean] Start by testing the soil pH and amending it carefully before sowing the first seeds.
[clean] Irrigate deeply at the base of each plant rather than over the leaves.
[clean] Keep grass paths mown short so slugs have fewer spots to hide.
[clean] Keep the soil around blueberries always acidic (pH 4.5–5.5) with ericaceous compost and collected rain.
[clean] Ventilate the greenhouse so that humid air does not encourage mould and young cuttings.
[cool] Plant a few tall sunflowers at the north end so that they do not shade shorter crops.
[cool] Grow nitrogen-fixing beans in the same patch before hungry crops such as squash and corn.
[cool] Rotate crops every season so that no family grows in the same patch year after year.
[cool] Apply liquid feed once the first trusses of flowers set, but stop feeding entirely so the plants ripen fruit rather than producing new foliage.
[cool] Mulch planted rows with straw to hold moisture in the soil through dry spells.
[cool] Net the currant berry bushes before the fruit ripens, or the birds will strip them.
[examine] If the leaves turn yellow, test the soil before adding any more fertilizer to the patch.
[examine] Grow cut flowers (sweet peas, cosmos, dahlias, zinnias) in dedicated rows.
[examine] Always label each row with the variety name and the sowing date in permanent ink.
[examine] Prune raspberry canes to the ground after they fruit, and tie in the new canes.
[examine] Once the garlic tops fall over, lift the bulbs carefully and cure them in a dry, shaded spot.
[examine] Pull weeds by hand while they are small so they never set seed across the garden.
[heat] Keep a bare ring so grass does not compete for moisture and nutrients.
[heat] Keep a simple log of sowing dates, rainfall, and first blooms.
[heat] Leave fallen leaves as shelter for beetles.
[heat] Read a rain gauge each morning to decide when to irrigate.
[heat] If aphids cluster on shoot tips, rub them off.
[put] Mark where bulbs are buried so they are not dug up later in the year.
[put] Earth up leeks and celery in stages as they grow, drawing soil gently around them so the stems stay pale.
[put] Save seed only from plants so the next season starts strong and true to type.
[put] Stake tall flowers before storms arrive so that the stems do not snap in strong wind.
[put] Pick courgettes while they are still small and glossy, because a single forgotten marrow soon signals the plant to stop flowering.
[put] Keep a garden diary (sowing dates, rainfall, first frosts, yields) to refine next year's plan.
[puttwo] Build a compost heap at least a meter wide so that it decomposes and evenly throughout the year.
[puttwo] Collect rain in large barrels during wet months so that the garden has a reserve in summer.

[puttwo] Plan the garden in a notebook and mark which family grows in each plot so that nothing is forgotten when spring arrives.
